items.t: Top 5 Companies With the Most Bonus Issues in India: Wipro Leads With 14 Bonus Issues
sum: Wipro leads Indian companies with 14 bonus issues, followed by L&T, Infosys, ITC and Cipla, highlighting their long-standing shareholder reward practices.

Bonus shares have remained a popular way for Indian companies to reward long-term shareholders. Instead of distributing cash, companies issue additional shares to existing investors without any extra cost. A bonus issue increases the number of shares held by investors, while the market price adjusts proportionately after the issue.

Companies generally announce bonus shares when they have accumulated reserves and want to improve stock liquidity, encourage retail participation and make their shares more accessible to investors. Over the years, several established companies across sectors have built a strong track record of rewarding shareholders through repeated bonus issues.

Among these companies, IT major Wipro leads the list with 14 bonus issues, followed by Larsen & Toubro (L&T) with 10 and Infosys with eight. FMCG major ITC and pharmaceutical company Cipla complete the top five, with seven bonus issues each.

Wipro has one of the longest bonus share histories among Indian listed companies. The company issued its first bonus shares in 1971 and has continued rewarding shareholders over several decades. According to historical bonus records, Wipro has announced 14 bonus issues, the highest among the companies featured in this list.

Its bonus issues include 1:3 in 1971, followed by 1:1 issues in 1981, 1985, 1987, 1989, 1992, 1995 and 2005. The company also announced 2:1 bonus issues in 1997 and 2004, a 2:3 issue in 2010, 1:1 in 2017, 1:3 in 2019 and 1:1 in 2024.

For example, under a 1:1 bonus issue, an investor holding 100 shares receives another 100 shares without any additional payment. The total holding increases to 200 shares. Similarly, an investor holding 500 shares receives 500 additional shares, taking the total holding to 1,000 shares. However, the market price adjusts proportionately after the bonus issue.

Earnings Miss: KEC International Limited Missed EPS By 76% And Analysts Are Revising Their Forecasts
sum: The analysts might have been a bit too bullish on KEC International Limited (NSE:KEC), given that the company fell short of expectations when it released its second-quarter results last week. It looks like quite a negative result overall, with both revenues and earnings falling well short of analyst predictions. Revenues of ₹55b missed by 11%, and statutory earnings per share of ₹1.12 fell short of forecasts by 76%. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

Following the latest results, KEC International's 25 analysts are now forecasting revenues of ₹259.9b in 2027. This would be a decent 13% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to expand 17% to ₹18.53. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of ₹259.9b and earnings per share (EPS) of ₹25.28 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become more bearish following the latest results. While there were no changes to revenue forecasts, there was a large cut to EPS estimates.

It might be a surprise to learn that the consensus price target was broadly unchanged at ₹513, with the analysts clearly implying that the forecast decline in earnings is not expected to have much of an impact on valuation. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. Currently, the most bullish analyst values KEC International at ₹635 per share, while the most bearish prices it at ₹318. This is a fairly broad spread of estimates, suggesting that analysts are forecasting a wide range of possible outcomes for the business.

Another way we can view these estimates is in the context of the bigger picture, such as how the forecasts stack up against past performance, and whether forecasts are more or less bullish relative to other companies in the industry.

Green Energy Stocks Surge As Renewable And Power Sector Shares Rally Across Indian Markets (04 November 2026)
sum: Indian equity markets closed on a positive note on November 4, 2026, supported by gains in benchmark indices and strong buying activity across green energy and power-related stocks. The S&P BSE SENSEX advanced 0.5% to close at 77,301.4 points, reflecting positive investor sentiment. Renewable energy companies, battery manufacturers, power utilities and other energy-sector stocks witnessed notable gains on both the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Insolation Energy emerged as one of the top performers in the renewable energy segment. Its shares surged 7.8% on the BSE to reach ₹73.35, while on the NSE, the stock gained 7.37% to trade at ₹73.15. Inox Wind also recorded strong buying interest, with its shares climbing 7.11% on the BSE to close at ₹63.57. The gains reflected positive trading activity across companies operating in India’s renewable energy infrastructure market.

Battery and energy storage companies also participated in the market rally. Exide Industries advanced 5.67% to ₹366.00 on the BSE, while Amara Raja Energy & Mobility gained nearly 4% to reach ₹724.50. Both companies have business interests in the battery and energy storage segments, which are attracting increasing attention amid the expansion of electric mobility and renewable energy integration.

Among major renewable energy developers, Adani Green Energy shares increased 3.45% to ₹1,381.10 on the BSE and 3.34% to ₹1,384.00 on the NSE. Borosil Renewables also gained 3.78% to trade at ₹393.00. Meanwhile, JSW Energy recorded a comparatively moderate increase of 1.59%, reaching ₹510.00 on the BSE.

Other energy and utility companies also recorded positive movements during the session. GAIL shares climbed 2.76% to ₹186.00, while Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) advanced 2.25% to ₹111.20 on the BSE. Indian Oil Corporation also witnessed buying activity, with its shares rising 2.53% to ₹142.00.
However, the market rally was not uniform across all major companies. Larsen & Toubro emerged among the notable laggards, declining marginally by 0.2% during the trading session.
The overall performance highlighted continued investor interest in India’s renewable energy and power sectors.

sum: Larsen & Toubro aims to boost revenue growth for its services arms, LTM and LTTS, to over 15%, leveraging AI disruption and strategic talent acquisition.

- L&T is leveraging layoffs at other companies to acquire high-tech talent and domain expertise.
- The company is focusing on finding new markets, particularly in the US and Europe, for its services businesses.
- L&T Finance is realigning its strategy towards retail lending and deploying significant technology in its operations.

Sensex, Nifty rise in early trade on Reliance buying, foreign inflows
sum: MUMBAI: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty rose in early trade on Thursday, driven by buying in blue-chip stock Reliance Industries and foreign fund inflows.
The 30-share BSE Sensex climbed 245.43 points, or 0.34 per cent, to 73,491.46 in morning trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty rose 62.55 points, or 0.28 per cent, to 22,761.40.
Adani Ports was the biggest gainer among Sensex constituents, rising 3 per cent after reporting an 18 per cent rise in consolidated net profit at Rs 3,682.44 crore for the quarter ended September.
Power Grid, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Titan, Reliance Industries, NTPC, Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Hindustan Unilever, ITC, and State Bank of India also traded in positive territory.
Trent, Maruti Suzuki India, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finserv, Larsen & Toubro, Tata Steel, HDFC Bank, Eternal and UltraTech Cement were among the laggards.
Shares of Jio Platforms Ltd extended gains for the second straight session after making a blockbuster debut on the exchanges a day earlier.
The stock of the company jumped over 5 per cent to Rs 1,490, taking the market capitalisation to Rs 13,72,145.59 crore.

Larsen & Toubro Q2 Results: Profit surges 33% YoY to Rs 5,202 crore, revenue grows 16%
sum: The engineering and construction major reported consolidated revenue of Rs 78,750 crore for the second quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), registering a 16% YoY growth from Rs 67,984 crore in the year-ago period.

The revenue growth was driven by accelerated progress across businesses in the Projects, Products and Manufacturing (PPM) portfolio. International revenue stood at Rs 45,870 crore during the quarter, accounting for 58% of the company's total revenue.

The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose marginally by around 0.6% YoY to Rs 6,845 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 6,806 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

For the half-year ended September 30, 2026, L&T reported consolidated revenue of Rs 1,46,692 crore, registering an 11% YoY growth. International revenue stood at Rs 80,263 crore, contributing 55% to the company's total revenue.

L&T secured orders worth Rs 1,47,665 crore during Q2FY27, registering a 28% YoY growth. The company won several high-value orders across its Hydrocarbon – Offshore and Onshore, CarbonLite Solutions, Public Spaces and Airports, and Power Transmission and Distribution businesses.

On a half-yearly basis, the company received orders worth Rs 2,55,678 crore, marking a 22% YoY increase. The growth was supported by strong order inflows across Hydrocarbon – Offshore, Offshore Wind, Minerals and Metals, and Residential and Commercial Buildings businesses.
International orders amounted to Rs 1,53,077 crore, contributing 60% to the total order inflow during the first half of FY27.
